clue.text: Stars settle for parts in Emmerdale Farm, perhaps

parts.note: the Plough is the star group also called the Big Dipper
to land is to come down and settle, as a bird does

explanation.surface: Celebrities settle for roles in a rural television soap.
explanation.walkthrough: Emmerdale Farm was a long-running British TV soap set on a Yorkshire farm; 'parts' of a farm here are its fields, not acting roles.
explanation.definitionFit: Arable fields on a farm are the acres turned by the plough, as any farm in the series would have.

clue.text: Apparently face being confined to bed?

definitions.text: Apparently face being confined to bed?

parts.words: Apparently face being confined to bed?
parts.note: someone lying in bed is placed with the face upwards, which is how an invalid is described

explanation.surface: Someone seemingly bedridden.
explanation.definitionFit: To be off sick and kept in bed by illness is to be bedridden for a while.

clue.text: His initials showing us the country he stands for

definitions.text: His initials showing us the country he stands for

parts.words: His initials showing us the country he stands for
parts.note: the figure's first letters are U and S, spelling the abbreviation of the nation he personifies

explanation.surface: A man whose monogram reveals the nation he represents.
explanation.definitionFit: This bearded cartoon figure in stars and stripes personifies the United States government.

clue.text: Upper class accommodated by prophet — gentleman of' this profession

definitions.text: Upper class accommodated by prophet — gentleman of' this profession

indicators.note: the second piece is housed inside the first

parts.note: Hosea is a minor prophet of the Old Testament
U is the old abbreviation for upper class
gent is short for gentleman

explanation.surface: Posh people housed by a seer: a man in the business of finding homes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accommodated by' puts U inside HOSEA, and the whole clue describes the job: finding upper-class clients somewhere to live.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate agent who lets and sells homes finds accommodation for clients, as the clue's whole picture shows.

clue.text: Bill needs a hair-piece — and Terry, for example?'

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: A man called Bill needs a wig, and so does Terry.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill and Terry look like two men, but Ellen Terry was a great Victorian stage performer.
explanation.definitionFit: Dame Ellen Terry was a celebrated stage performer of the late nineteenth century.

clue.text: Acts of females

explanation.surface: Deeds of women.
explanation.definitionFit: Does is a verb for performs; and female deer, rabbits and hares are called by the same word.

clue.text: Declare girl put on weight

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name
an ounce is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: Say publicly that a young woman has gained weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put on weight' reads as getting fatter, but 'put on' places ANN above OUNCE.
explanation.definitionFit: To announce is to make something known publicly, to proclaim.

clue.text: Law not enforced of late permissive type

parts.note: late means dead, as in the late king
a letter is one who lets, or allows

explanation.surface: A rule that no one applies, from a lenient person recently in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: A statute still on the books but no longer acted on is described with this phrase.

clue.text: Shady house, William's?

explanation.surface: A dark dwelling belonging to a man called William.
explanation.walkthrough: William III of England was William of Orange, from the Dutch royal house of that name.
explanation.definitionFit: The colour is one shade of the spectrum, hence 'shady'; and the Dutch royal dynasty of King William III bears the same name.

clue.text: Figure is put to one nobleman or another

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral five, a figure
a count is a continental nobleman

explanation.surface: A number is attached to one aristocrat or some other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' is the definition: the answer is a further rank of nobleman beside the count.
explanation.definitionFit: A viscount ranks just above a baron in the peerage, a different titled lord from a count.

clue.text: Bloomer made by conductor it's in piano pieces, perhaps

parts.note: a rose is a flower, something that blooms
Sir Henry Wood was the conductor who founded the Proms concerts

explanation.surface: A conductor's blunder turns up among his piano music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a mistake but is a flower; 'piano pieces' are the wooden parts of a piano, not compositions.
explanation.definitionFit: This dark tropical timber is used for the cases and parts of fine pianos.

clue.text: Work thus holds up retirement

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the whole is read from right to left
the first word placed around the second, holding it

parts.note: so means thus, in this way

explanation.surface: Labour in this way delays someone stopping work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds up' reads as delaying, but 'holds' is the container and 'up' gives its own letters; 'retirement' turns the result backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A composer's numbered composition is called a work, as in Beethoven's Op. 27.

clue.text: Narcotic ' put outside for transport what infamy!

indicators.note: the drug's letters are placed around the other pieces

parts.note: opium is a narcotic drug
pro means for, in favour of
BR, British Rail, the old national railway, is transport

explanation.surface: A drug is placed outside for carrying away: what a disgrace!
explanation.walkthrough: 'put outside' reads as taking the drug out of doors; it wraps the drug around the other two pieces. BR stood for British Rail, Britain's former state railway.
explanation.definitionFit: Opprobrium is public disgrace and scorn, the shame that infamy brings.

clue.text: TT riders' practice?

parts.note: looks like training for the Isle of Man TT motorcycle races; TT also means teetotal, so it is the habit of non-drinkers

explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Man TT is a famous motorcycle road race; TT is also short for teetotal.
explanation.definitionFit: Refraining from alcohol is the way of life of teetotallers.

clue.text: Saving person's property in siege?

explanation.surface: Rescuing someone's belongings during a blockade.
explanation.walkthrough: To invest a town is to besiege it, so the noun also means a siege; money put by is the everyday sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Money put by to grow is saved capital; and the word is an old military term for blockading a town.

clue.text: The first of ten?

parts.note: the leading one, and the head of government who lives at Number Ten Downing Street

explanation.walkthrough: The British Prime Minister lives at 10 Downing Street.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means first or foremost, and is also a name for the Prime Minister, whose home is Number Ten.

clue.text: Judge investing one thousand in landed property

indicators.note: the pieces sit inside the landed property word

parts.note: an estate is land owned by someone
I is the Roman numeral one
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: A judge putting a grand into a country property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'investing' seems to be the judge putting money in, but it only links; 'in' puts I and M inside ESTATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To estimate is to judge or reckon a value roughly.

clue.text: This was mounted in time for the Coronation

definitions.text: This was mounted in time for the Coronation

parts.words: This was mounted in time for the Coronation
parts.note: something set up for a ceremony, but in fact a peak climbed, with the news arriving on the day Elizabeth II was crowned

explanation.surface: Something was put up just ready for the crowning of the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: Hillary and Tenzing reached the summit in May 1953, and the news broke on Coronation Day, 2 June 1953.
explanation.definitionFit: The world's highest mountain was first climbed days before Queen Elizabeth II was crowned.

clue.text: Fugitive from rail union upset old dramatic critic

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the letters run from the bottom

parts.note: NUR was the National Union of Railwaymen in Britain
James Agate was a famous British theatre critic of the 1920s to 1940s

explanation.surface: A runaway from the railway workers upsets a veteran theatre reviewer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns NUR into RUN.
explanation.definitionFit: A runagate is an archaic word for a deserter or runaway.

clue.text: Mistake in the name of a gas

indicators.note: mistaking the letters means getting them out of order

explanation.surface: An error in what a gas is called.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mistake in' rearranges THE NAME.
explanation.definitionFit: Methane is the main component of natural gas, a flammable hydrocarbon.

clue.text: Strike call for mechanics or equipment suppliers

parts.note: 'out!' is the cry calling workers out on strike
fitters are mechanics who assemble machinery

explanation.surface: A union calls a walkout for the engineers, or for the firms supplying kit.
explanation.definitionFit: Outfitters are shops selling clothing and gear for an activity.

clue.text: Mean side of driver?

explanation.surface: A stingy streak in a motorist.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the nearside of a car is the kerb side, away from the driver; the old sense of the word is also stingy.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an old term for stingy; and the nearside is the side of a vehicle closest to the kerb.

clue.text: Turkish commander gets free lift in Morocco

parts.note: an aga was an Ottoman military commander

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting the word raises it so it reads upwards

parts.note: to rid is to free

explanation.surface: An Ottoman officer gets a free ride in North Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lift' looks like a ride but turns RID upwards to DIR.
explanation.definitionFit: Agadir is a port city on the Atlantic coast of Morocco.

clue.text: Odd blow could put you under the table?

definitions.text: could put you under the table?

parts.note: rum is old British slang for odd or strange
a punch is a blow

explanation.surface: A strange punch might floor you.
explanation.walkthrough: To drink someone under the table is to outlast them in drinking until they collapse; 'blow' suggests a knockout.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong spirit-based mixed drink can leave a drinker sprawled on the floor.

clue.text: Sisters of joshua's father

explanation.surface: Female siblings belonging to the parent of Joshua.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Bible, Joshua is called the son of Nun.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of a religious order of women are called Sisters; and the possessive of the name of Joshua's biblical father gives the same letters.

clue.text: Set in a river in Australia

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the first piece sits inside the others

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland, and another in Wales and England
laid means set down

explanation.surface: Placed in a river down under.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set' looks like the definition, but it supplies the inner piece; the closing 'in Australia' is the definition of a state capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Adelaide is the capital city of South Australia.

clue.text: Building now put in residential area of New York?

indicators.note: building means constructing something new from these letters

explanation.surface: A building has just been put up in a Manhattan neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Building' rearranges NOW PUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Uptown is the American term for the residential district away from downtown, as in upper Manhattan.

clue.text: Lover of course needing courage

parts.note: the sweet is the dessert course of a meal
heart means courage

explanation.surface: A lover, naturally, needs to be brave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' reads as 'naturally', but 'course' is a meal course.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweetheart is a beloved partner, a person in love.
